papers.abstractEn: Representing individual-level behavioral heterogeneity is challenging in epidemiological modeling, particularly when empirical behavioral data are sparse. We assess the potential of large language model (LLM)-generated behavioral outputs in addressing this challenge, using hepatitis C virus-related behaviors among people who inject drugs as a case study. Correspondence with epidemiological patterns was evaluated using external benchmarks: literature-informed association directions, correlations from an agent-based model (ABM), and survey associations. Across three LLMs, unconditional directional recovery across 28 retained literature-informed associations was 46-68%, compared with 82-93% agreement when LLMs were directly asked to classify the same associations. Mean absolute differences from ABM and survey correlation patterns were 0.11-0.13 and 0.15-0.18, respectively. Together, these findings show partial alignment between LLM-generated behavioral relationships and epidemiological evidence, despite higher knowledge-probe agreement. More systematic evaluation is needed before incorporating LLM-generated behavioral outputs into epidemiological models that simulate transmission dynamics.

classification.tldr: 以丙肝相关行为为案例，用文献关联、基于主体模型和调查数据等外部基准系统评估大语言模型生成行为模式与流行病学证据的一致性，发现仅部分对齐。

papers.title: Large language model-generated patterns for epidemiological modeling: a multi-benchmark evaluation framework

papers.abstractEn: Curriculum teams often lack time to check whether assigned readings support learning objectives (LOs) and whether topic coverage is balanced. We present a natural language processing (NLP) workflow to support evidence-informed curation of reading lists. The workflow combines PubMedBERT sentence embeddings and cosine similarity for retrieval, natural language inference (NLI) for evidence checking, and topic modeling for coverage analysis. We tested the approach in dental education using 13 course-level LOs and a PubMed-derived corpus of 3,837 LO-abstract pairs. Median cosine similarity ranged from 0.86 to 0.91 across the 13 LOs, showing generally high semantic similarity. Topic modeling showed broad but uneven coverage, with one or two dominant topics per domain. Similarity alone was not enough for selecting readings: among high-similarity pairs (cosine 0.90-1.00), 22.9% were classified by NLI as neutral or contradictory. In a 49-pair expert-labeled validation set, cosine-based retrieval (cosine >= 0.90) achieved 0.69 accuracy, while the combined cosine and NLI approach achieved 0.73 accuracy against expert alignment labels. Overall, the workflow shows how AI can support curriculum alignment by reducing false positives and helping select readings that better match intended LOs.

classification.tldr: 该文构建了结合句子嵌入检索、自然语言推理校验与主题建模的NLP工作流，用于牙医学教育中课程阅读材料与教学目标的对齐评估，实验显示融合NLI可降低误报并提升对齐判断准确率。

papers.title: Natural Language Processing for Aligning Readings with Learning Objectives and Assessing Topic Balance in Dental Education

papers.abstractEn: Large language models (LLMs) have shown considerable promise in clinical decision support. However, existing approaches often rely on multi-step reasoning or multi-agent collaboration to execute clinical guidelines, introducing substantial computational overhead without reliably preventing decision errors. To address these limitations, we propose a framework for Medical Decision Execution (MedDEx) that integrates structured patient states with deterministic rule execution to support guideline-based treatment planning. MedDEx separates clinical record interpretation from guideline execution, leveraging LLMs to extract patient information and generate treatment plans while assigning guideline-defined decision logic to a rule executor. Experiments across multiple clinical guideline benchmarks demonstrate that MedDEx improves decision accuracy while reducing inference costs. Further analyses highlight the critical roles of structured patient representations and deterministic rule execution, suggesting that additional LLM reasoning does not necessarily translate into better guideline adherence.

classification.tldr: 论文提出将LLM信息抽取与确定性规则执行分离的临床指南执行框架MedDEx，实验表明结构化患者状态加规则执行比更多LLM推理步数在准确性和推理成本上均更优。

papers.title: More Reasoning Is Not Always Better: Executing Clinical Guidelines with LLMs and Rules

papers.abstractEn: Healthcare agents must transform longitudinal clinical evidence into reliable actions through heterogeneous tools and stateful workflows, conditions under which model-centric systems may lose context, misuse tools, fail to verify consequential transitions, or cross authorization boundaries. Existing medical-agent benchmarks primarily emphasize terminal task outcomes, making it difficult to determine whether execution failures arise from the agent model, the runtime harness, or their interaction. We present the Medical Harness Protocol, an outcome-preserving framework that independently evaluates seven healthcare-specific process dimensions: Care Action Fulfillment, Clinical Resource Competence, Patient-Evidence Alignment, Clinical Workflow Continuity, Clinical Auditability, Closed-Loop Verification, and Clinical Conduct Boundaries. A normalized intervention trace further tracks whether runtime support is available, activated, delivered, adopted by the agent, and propagated into subsequent behavior. We instantiate the protocol as MedHarnessBench, comprising 342 executable tasks across FHIR/EHR operations, healthcare-administration interfaces, and multimodal clinical tools. Across more than 16,000 controlled task executions, MedHarness yields broad improvements in terminal task success, intermediate subtask completion, and healthcare-specific process quality. We further evaluate MedHarness against multiple general-purpose harnesses and use controlled single-fault perturbations to verify the sensitivity and discrimination of the seven-dimensional evaluation. These results demonstrate that healthcare-specific runtime support can substantially improve both task completion and execution quality, while revealing failures that terminal outcomes alone cannot capture. Code and resources are available at https://github.com/Tomry1114/Awesome-Agent-Harness-for-Healthcare.

classification.tldr: 发布医疗智能体评测基准MedHarnessBench，从七个过程维度独立评估医疗智能体执行质量，验证专用运行时支持可显著提升任务成功率。

papers.title: MedHarnessBench: A Unified Benchmark for Healthcare Agent Evaluation

papers.abstractEn: Respiratory auscultation provides a low-cost means of assessing pulmonary function, yet transient crackles and sustained wheezes can be difficult to recognize in noisy clinical recordings. Conventional deep learning classifiers often operate as black boxes, offering limited insight into the temporal acoustic evidence supporting their predictions. We present RespFocus, a weakly supervised framework that uses multiple instance learning (MIL) to learn inspectable temporal evidence from cycle-level labels and integrate it into classification. We also introduce PedResp2026, a multicenter pediatric respiratory sound cohort collected in routine clinical environments with adjudicated cycle-level annotations. In classification experiments, RespFocus achieves four-class Scores of 69.55\% on public ICBHI 2017 and 72.91\% on PedResp2026. Evidence diagnostics and matched temporal interventions support the functional contribution of the learned evidence to model predictions. Together, these findings highlight RespFocus's potential as a tool for automated respiratory sound diagnosis.

classification.tldr: 本文提出弱监督的多示例学习框架，从呼吸音中学习可检视的时序证据用于分类，并发布多中心儿科呼吸音数据集，在公开与自建数据集上取得较好效果。

papers.title: RespFocus: Learning Temporal Evidence for Weakly Supervised Respiratory Sound Classification

papers.abstractEn: Large language models can produce fluent tu- toring dialogue, but whether they actually help students learn remains unclear. We present a process-centered synthesis of LLM tutoring that follows the path from learner-state infer- ence to pedagogical action, tutor training, eval- uation, and student simulation. This view ex- poses a central gap: implementing a tutoring component does not establish that it works or that its outputs meaningfully affect later stages. A structured study-level audit shows that peda- gogical evaluation is common, while evidence becomes much thinner for learner-conditioned intervention, human learning gains, and espe- cially transfer or delayed retention. Human studies nevertheless provide a conditional posi- tive result: LLM tutors can improve learning, but benefits depend on pedagogical structure, learner engagement, and how learning is mea- sured. We argue that progress requires validat- ing the interfaces between tutoring stages, not only improving individual components.

classification.tldr: 对LLM家教系统进行以过程为中心的综述审计，发现各组件实现与教学效果验证之间存在明显缺口，学习收益依赖教学结构和测量方式。

papers.title: Do LLM Tutors Actually Teach? A Process-Centered Synthesis of the Tutoring Loop

papers.abstractEn: Materials synthesis planning (MSP) connects AI-driven materials discovery to experimental realization by proposing precursors, synthesis operations, and processing conditions for a target material. Existing approaches predict these components separately or in pairs and treat conditions only as a prediction target. Consequently, MSP remains centered on recipe prediction: it leaves unexplored how conditions can serve as process context for constructing synthesis routes, and it does not address which candidate routes should be executed under limited experimental resources. We propose CondMSP, which extends MSP from recipe prediction to execution-aware planning. CondMSP predicts temperature, time, and atmosphere by combining a joint predictor with variable-specific experts, and then uses these predictions both as process context, grounding the generation and retrieval of operation sequences, and as execution requirements, specifying which thermal stages can share a furnace run and at what cost. This specification is held fixed across all compared methods; within it, CondMSP ranks routes across precursor sets by a common utility and, under furnace budgets, jointly selects routes and allocates their thermal stages by constrained optimization. CondMSP improves condition and operation prediction and, under this shared constraint, raises reference-recipe recovery from 27.9% to 32.9% at three simulated furnace runs per target and from 34.7% to 40.0% at 30 trials, while a new evaluation set of 2,344 targets supports generalization beyond oxide-dominated training chemistry.

classification.tldr: 该论文提出面向无机材料合成的条件感知规划方法，将合成条件预测同时用作过程上下文与执行约束，并在炉次预算下通过约束优化联合选择合成路线与分配热处理阶段，提升了配方恢复率。

papers.title: CondMSP: Condition-Informed and Resource-Aware Inorganic Materials Synthesis Planning

papers.abstractEn: Safety-aligned large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to adversarial prompts that bypass their safety training. Existing automated red-teaming methods either require privileged access unavailable in production, rely on manually engineered per-model templates, or optimize a single objective without population-level diversity. We present REPRO (Reflective Evolutionary Prompt Optimization), a pure black-box framework that discovers adversarial prompts through evolutionary optimization driven entirely by a compressed open-weight 7B reflective model on a single consumer GPU. REPRO introduces two mechanisms absent from prior work, both isolated in a component ablation: semantic crossover, an LLM-guided multi-parent recombination operator, and Bayesian strategy selection via Thompson Sampling informed by structured failure analysis. We catalog REPRO's behavior on AdvBench, JailbreakBench, and HarmBench across 36 target models from 11 families, including GPT-5-nano, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Gemini-2.5-Pro, and Grok-4.1. Under our protocol REPRO reaches 100\% attack success rate (ASR) on every evaluated target in a single turn, at a median of 24 target queries per behavior. Two properties of the protocol qualify that figure. The judge scoring candidates during optimization also produces the reported ASR, and search halts when it accepts, so ASR reports whether search succeeded within the iteration budget rather than success at a fixed budget. All baseline figures are transcribed from their original papers, which use different judges, budgets, and model versions. We therefore present this as a catalog of model coverage under one protocol rather than a head-to-head ranking, and develop both qualifications in the paper.

classification.tldr: 论文提出纯黑盒进化式提示优化框架REPRO，用7B反思模型在单卡GPU上自动化红队测试，在36个目标模型上达成高攻击成功率。

papers.title: REPRO: Reflective Evolutionary Prompt Optimizer for Automated LLM Red-Teaming

papers.abstractEn: Accurate, physiologically consistent glucose forecasts could help people with type 1 diabetes respond to impending excursions. We applied our physiological-model-based neural network (PMB--NN) framework to glucose forecasting. A temporal convolutional network (TCN) used 180 min of history, constrained during training by a personalized four-parameter physiological model. The main PMB--NN combined forecast and neural--physiological agreement losses; a three-term variant additionally fitted physiological predictions to measured glucose. Data comprised 6--8 weeks of continuous glucose monitoring, pump, and meal records from 25 AZT1D participants. Person-specific models used chronological 70/10/20 train/validation/test splits and 30-, 60-, and 120-min horizons. Median mean absolute errors were 16.24, 25.00, and 30.20 mg/dL with basal insulin records and 15.38, 24.21, and 31.79 mg/dL before these records became available. In the latter setting, PMB--NN had the lowest median error at 30 and 60 min; it outperformed the physiological model alone in all six settings. In input-increase tests, glucose predictions changed in the expected direction for 85\% of correction boluses and 100\% of carbohydrate rescues, versus 57\% for active insulin and 56\% for active carbohydrates. Most standalone physiological fits showed locally distinguishable parameter effects, with glucose-related coefficients more stable under resampling than insulin- or carbohydrate-related coefficients. The three-term variant improved hyperglycaemia accuracy with basal records, but did not significantly change overall MAE and reduced directional plausibility in three tests. PMB--NN combines personalized forecasting with an explicit physiological model, allowing assessment of predictive accuracy, physiological response behavior, and participant-specific coefficients.

classification.tldr: 将个性化生理模型作为约束融入神经网络，用于1型糖尿病患者的血糖预测，在多个预测时域上取得更低误差且预测方向更符合生理预期。

papers.title: Personalized Physiological-Model-Based Neural Network for Glucose Forecasting in Type 1 Diabetes

papers.abstractEn: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) diagnosis remains challenging due to heterogeneous symptoms and reliance on clinical assessment, underscoring the need for objective, data-driven approaches that leverage patient-generated physiological signals. We propose Siam-ALS, an explainable Siamese deep learning framework that jointly models synchronized electroencephalography (EEG) and eye-tracking (ET) signals. EEG captures ALS-related changes in brain activity, while ET provides information about oculomotor control, allowing the model to learn complementary patterns associated with ALS. The framework employs two modality-specific encoders: a convolutional EEG encoder that captures spatiotemporal neural patterns and an MLP-based ET encoder that models oculomotor dynamics. These modality-specific features are processed through weight-sharing Siamese branches and fused into a compact 64-dimensional joint embedding. A lightweight classifier is used to predict ALS, while pairwise metric learning helps the model learn more effective patterns from the small, diverse ALS datasets. Performance was evaluated on the public EEGET-ALS dataset using strict subject-level cross-validation, where Siam-ALS achieved an accuracy of 0.988 and an AUROC of 0.998, demonstrating strong performance compared with classical machine learning, DL, and non-Siamese fusion approaches. Cross-dataset evaluation on the independent BigP3BCI dataset achieved an AUROC of approximately 0.98, supporting the generalization capability of Siam-ALS across different BCI paradigms. To enhance interpretability, six XAI methods were evaluated in the learned embedding space, with SHAP achieving the highest, though statistically comparable, fidelity in identifying important EEG and ET patterns that contribute to ALS predictions. Overall, Siam-ALS provides an accurate, generalizable, and explainable framework for multimodal ALS detection.

classification.tldr: 提出可解释的孪生深度学习框架Siam-ALS，联合建模EEG与眼动信号进行ALS早期检测，在跨数据集评估中达到约0.98的AUROC并具备良好泛化能力。

papers.title: Siam-ALS: An Explainable Siamese Deep Learning Framework for Early ALS Detection Using EEG and Eye-Tracking Signals

papers.abstractEn: The inherent variability of fMRI responses across trials encourages a generative view of the stimulus-to-response mapping. Prior generative encoders often operate in compressed latent spaces and condition predominantly on semantic features, which provide limited low-level cues for early visual cortex. We propose StimFlow, which synthesizes fMRI directly in native voxel space using conditional flow matching with a linear path. This design aligns training and inference distributions, enabling competitive performance with a single sample and reducing reliance on averaging. To match the visual hierarchy, StimFlow combines structural DINOv2 features with semantic CLIP features, which prove complementary along the cortical processing stream. With a single sample, StimFlow achieves a per-voxel Pearson correlation of 0.371, matching baselines that average five draws. Generation in voxel space allows direct ROI analysis and concept localization without a decoder. Furthermore, it recovers over half of full-data performance from just one hour of scans, supporting efficient cross-subject adaptation.

classification.tldr: 提出在原始体素空间用条件流匹配从图像直接合成fMRI的方法，单样本即可匹配多采样基线，并支持低数据量的跨被试高效适配。

papers.title: StimFlow: Synthesizing Brain Activity from Images via Stimulus-conditioned Flow Matching

papers.abstractEn: Current fMRI encoding models frame prediction as deterministic regression, yet identical stimuli evoke a distribution of neural responses (arising from physiological noise, hemodynamic variability, and cognitive fluctuations) that a single point estimate cannot capture. This work introduces MultiFlow, a generative fMRI encoding framework based on Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) and a formulation termed Stimulus-Informed Source Flow Matching (SISFM). SISFM generalises CFM by conditioning the source distribution on the stimulus: a learnable temporal convolution shapes the source mean with an HRF-length receptive field, while a variance head shrinks its scale, shortening the expected transport path. SISFM is instantiated with a Diffusion Transformer (DiT-X) decoder parameterising the velocity field, with sub-layer Attention Residuals, heterogeneous fusion of ten frozen vision, audio, language, and audiovisual backbones, and per-subject Yeo-network heads. On the Algonauts 2025 dataset, a single MultiFlow checkpoint recovers most of the benefit of large deterministic ensembles: it trails the 1000-model TRIBE ensemble in-distribution by 0.003 PCC (0.3163 vs. 0.3195), and the strongest in- and out-of-distribution ensembles (VIBE-20, MedARC-50) by 0.010 and 0.009 PCC, using a single trained model rather than an ensemble of 20-1000. The same checkpoint also provides stimulus-conditioned uncertainty estimates and sample-based diversity.

classification.tldr: 提出基于条件流匹配的生成式fMRI编码框架，将源分布以多模态刺激为条件，用单一模型接近大规模确定性集成模型的脑活动预测性能。

papers.title: MultiFlow: Vision-Driven Multimodal fMRI Encoding via Stimulus-Informed Source Flow Matching

papers.abstractEn: Large language models (LLMs) offer a new approach to wearable-sensor-based human activity recognition. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) further introduces similar motion examples and discriminative sensor knowledge, enabling decisions grounded in observations relevant to the current query. More evidence, however, does not necessarily mean better-organized evidence. When online prompts and LLM agents primarily orchestrate inference, decisions about which activities to compare and when to invoke discriminative knowledge remain concentrated at inference time. As the activity vocabulary grows, the model must repeatedly process more candidates and associated knowledge, whereas pruning candidates too early risks excluding the true activity. We propose confusion-hierarchy evidence-aware reasoning (CHEAR), which moves part of this knowledge organization offline. CHEAR constructs and validates an activity hierarchy from recurrent cross-subject retrieval errors and builds corresponding activity-pair knowledge. At inference time, the hierarchy orders candidate comparisons; the LLM retains candidates progressively, and local discriminative knowledge is accessed only for the remaining activities. Across eight datasets, CHEAR achieves 86.79\% mean cross-subject accuracy, a 75.91\% candidate reduction rate, and 96.44\% true-activity retention. Per-sample token use is 85.15\% lower on average than in a variant without the hierarchical structure. Mean accuracy across eight cross-dataset transfer directions is 88.81\%. These results show that organizing candidates and discriminative knowledge around observed activity confusions reduces online LLM input while maintaining recognition performance.

classification.tldr: 提出将活动混淆层级知识离线组织的RAG推理方法，通过分层剪枝候选和按需调用判别知识，在保持识别精度的同时大幅降低在线LLM的token开销。

papers.title: CHEAR: Confusion-Hierarchy Evidence-Aware Reasoning for Cost-Efficient Human Activity Recognition

papers.abstractEn: LLMs increasingly support sensor-based human activity recognition (HAR) by linking motion signals with activity semantics and physical knowledge. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounds decisions in sensor examples and domain features, enabling training-free target-user inference with less dependence on raw numerical arrays. However, existing LLM/RAG-based HAR typically searches single-level activity spaces using static population knowledge. Consequently, they compare many unrelated candidates using the same static population evidence and overlook personalized motion patterns. We propose OntoAR-HAR, an ontology-guided agentic RAG framework combining static population and personalized knowledge. Its tree-structured activity ontology decomposes classification into local decisions among semantically related activities. The static store supplies node-constrained examples, while offline-discovered executable signal features provide numerical evidence for local distinctions. During inference, the personalized store collects selected user observations, which the LLM integrates with static knowledge and signal features while traversing the ontology to an activity label. Cross-subject and heterogeneous-sensing experiments show complementary gains from hierarchical retrieval and personalized memory across multiple LLM backbones, achieving state-of-the-art performance. By explicitly modeling hierarchical relations across activity granularities, OntoAR-HAR also addresses the long-overlooked semantic inclusion problem and avoids treating related labels as independent categories.

classification.tldr: 提出本体引导的分层RAG框架，结合静态种群知识与个性化记忆进行可穿戴传感器的人类活动识别，在跨被试和异构传感实验中取得最优性能。

papers.title: OntoAR-HAR: Ontology-Guided Agentic RAG with Personalized Memory for Human Activity Recognition

papers.abstractEn: Most benchmarks for large language models in medicine are built from licensing examinations and theoretical questions. The few that draw on real clinical data do so only in part, and rarely require a model to read a patient's own imaging. ClinEdge addresses this gap with 32 real, de-identified patient cases from active clinical practice, each evaluated across seven frontier systems for a total of 224 expert-graded evaluations. Each case pairs primary imaging with a short vignette, contains a feature known to defeat pattern-matched reasoning, and is scored against the patient's documented clinical course. The suite is built for depth rather than volume. Grading followed a two-stage expert process. First, a senior orthopaedic surgeon graded all 224 responses on a weighted rubric and a pass-or-fail verdict. Second, a panel of nineteen physicians, largely senior specialists at teaching medical colleges, independently reviewed every case and every one of the 224 grades. All seven production systems were evaluated through their public interfaces, and all 224 conversations are preserved as replayable links. Performance was poor across all systems, and the failures were shared: different vendors missed the same findings and converged on the same wrong plans. From the experts' notes we catalogue 18 recurring failure modes in five families. The models stop reading an image at the first finding. They give generic plans and lean toward over-treatment. They trust a misleading history over correct imaging. Their answers vary across systems and runs, and change with question format. Failing answers were delivered fluently and without any expressed uncertainty. Four cases are released in full; the remaining 28 are held out, and we invite frontier AI labs and healthcare AI companies to evaluate their models against them (research@futrbridge.com)

classification.tldr: 发布基于32个真实骨科边缘病例、由224次专家双阶段评分的多模态医疗基准，发现七个前沿模型表现均差且失败模式趋同，并归纳出18类反复出现的错误模式。

papers.title: ClinEdge: An Expert-Graded Benchmark of Real Patient Edge Cases Where Frontier Multimodal Models Fail

papers.abstractEn: Condensed matter stands to gain profoundly from widespread adoption of artificial intelligence (AI). However, its current means of data organization impedes this endeavor. As a premier measure of electronic structure underlying material properties, Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES) has accumulated over four decades of spectra, yet the community's publication-centered workflow preserves only a highly selected fraction of its experimental record. A shared data ecosystem could transform these fragmented measurements and their contexts into a persistent, collective scientific memory, creating immediate value for reproducibility and reuse while laying the foundation for AI-enabled discovery. In this Perspective, we report outcomes of a recent community workshop and propose a practical path toward such an ecosystem. Its benefits unfold along three timescales. In the near term, standardized, searchable, and citable datasets strengthen analysis pipelines independently of AI. In the intermediate future, community-validated tools operating across laboratories could enable broader reuse and increasingly closed-loop automated experiments. In the long term, a diverse corpus of measured electronic spectra could support foundation models for quantum matter. Looking forward, a diverse corpus of measured electronic spectra could support foundation models for quantum matter and new discoveries. We discuss lessons from existing scientific databases, the current state of AI in ARPES, as well as areas of community convergence on data organization, access, credit, governance, and a staged pilot program.

classification.tldr: 基于社区研讨提出构建AI就绪的ARPES电子结构数据库生态的分阶段路线，以标准化、可检索、可引用的数据共享支撑可复现分析和未来的量子物质基础模型。

papers.title: Framework for an AI-Ready ARPES Community Database

papers.abstractEn: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) models, particularly large language models (LLMs), are increasingly used in educational settings for tasks such as item generation, automated scoring, and feedback delivery. The quality of these outputs depends not only on the AI model but also on how users construct the prompts that guide model behaviors. Current prompt engineering practices are largely ad hoc, relying on trial and error rather than principled design. This lack of structure introduces validity threats including construct misrepresentation, construct-irrelevant variance, and limited reproducibility. We propose that Evidence-Centered Design (ECD), a framework in educational measurement for structuring valid inferences from observed performance, can serve as a principled foundation for prompt engineering in educational applications. We map the three core ECD models, the student model, the evidence model, and the task model, onto the components of educational prompt design, and describe a workflow for ECD-based prompt engineering. We derive five design principles from this mapping and present an empirical study contrasting ECD-designed prompts with state-of-the-art (SOTA) prompting baselines on an automated scoring task. Our empirical study demonstrates the usefulness of this framework on automated scoring. Results suggest that treating prompting as assessment design rather than informal instructions strengthens the validity, reliability, and fairness of AI-generated educational outputs.

classification.tldr: 将教育测量中的证据中心设计框架引入提示工程，提出五条设计原则和工作流程，在自动作文评分实验中证明其比现有提示基线更能提升AI输出的效度、信度与公平性。

papers.title: Using Evidence-Centered Design to Guide Prompt Engineering in Measurement: An Illustration with Automated Essay Scoring

papers.abstractEn: Efficient task scheduling in heterogeneous computing systems remains a fundamental challenge in embedded and high-level synthesis flows. This paper presents MoSAIC (Motif-aware Scheduling with AI-driven Cognition), a learning-based framework that bridges the gap between exact and heuristic scheduling approaches for DAG-based applications. The system uses the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) to learn the relationships between DAG structures and scheduling priority functions. The framework first leverages the OR-Tools CP-SAT solver [4] to generate optimal schedules, which are then used to supervise the learning of compact priority-based scheduling functions through Bayesian Optimization. These learned heuristics capture relationships between scheduling decisions and structural graph features such as rank, depth, and fanout, enabling the construction of a reusable knowledge base across diverse DAG instances. Experimental results across synthetic graph families and real-world benchmarks, including PolyBench and MachSuite, show that the learned heuristics consistently improve over classical approaches such as HEFT [2], while maintaining low runtime overhead. The results indicate that combining optimal supervision with learning-based generalization provides a practical approach for scalable and adaptive task scheduling.

classification.tldr: 该论文提出利用LLM推理能力从最优调度中学习DAG任务调度启发式的框架，以精确求解器作监督并构建可复用的结构知识库，在多个基准上稳定优于HEFT等经典方法。

papers.title: MoSAIC: Learning DAG Scheduling Heuristics from Optimal Schedules through Motif-Aware Recovery and LLM-Guided Reasoning

papers.abstractEn: Large language models are increasingly used in computer science education. However, the teaching abilities of even the most powerful LLMs are limited: they tend to reveal the solution prematurely and may lose focus on the learner's current debugging objective. To address this, we introduce SocraticRepair, a planning-guided Socratic tutoring framework for program debugging and miscon- ception repair that adapts prior planning-guided tutoring work (Li et al., 2026b). The framework is instantiated in the Python programming domain by fine-tuning Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct on synthetic multi-turn tutoring dialogues constructed from four preprocessed programming datasets. The system is evaluated using a predefined set of independent metrics and benchmarked against a general-purpose LLM. The experiments show that SocraticRepair achieves higher scores on stepwise scaffolding and question quality while also substantially reducing premature solution disclosure. The results also identify reliable pedagogical plan generation as an important remaining challenge.

classification.tldr: 该论文面向程序调试教学提出规划引导的苏格拉底式辅导框架，通过在合成的多轮辅导对话上微调代码模型，提高逐步引导与提问质量并显著减少过早泄露答案。

papers.title: SocraticRepair: Planning-Guided Socratic Tutoring for Program Debugging and Misconception Repair

papers.abstractEn: Batch risk-based inspection scheduling struggles to detect a critical failure class: food facilities with recent clean inspections that subsequently develop severe violations. Traditional systems recompute risk on fixed planning cycles using static historical data, leaving blind spots between inspection cycles. To address this, we introduce the Continuous Inspection Risk (CIR) system, an event-driven scheduling pipeline that re-ranks the inspection queue dynamically as new data arrives. CIR combines a decay-weighted historical score with a stream of real-time consumer reviews triaged by a language-model classifier. A key structural contribution is our temporal partition rule, which strictly excludes reviews predating the most recent inspection to prevent superseded signals from skewing current risk. Evaluating CIR on 9,505 routine inspections in Santa Clara County, California (2024-2026), we show that history-based scoring alone reduces mean time-to-detection of major violations by 69 days (20.9%) under a 30% inspection budget, but fails to anticipate severe vermin-related closures (0/8 detected). Incorporating post-inspection review signals drastically improves performance, predicting 7 of 8 vermin closures with an average lead time of 117 days-firing on the exact day of review publication in four instances. Introducing a review corroboration rule improves precision from 0.70 to 0.78 without loss of recall. Finally, we analyze critical implementation challenges, documenting a data-hygiene pitfall (stale review leakage across inspection boundaries) and an evaluation limitation involving unobserved facility self-remediation. This work provides the first case-level evaluation of event-driven inspection triggering using open data and provides a reproducible benchmark for review-augmented public health systems

classification.tldr: 提出基于事件的连续食品安全检查风险调度系统CIR，结合衰减历史评分与语言模型分类的实时消费者评论信号，将严重违规的检出提前约117天。

papers.title: Continuous Risk-Based Scheduling for Food Safety Inspection: Integrating Historical Decay with Event-Driven Consumer Review Signals

papers.abstractEn: Trust calibration remains the dominant framing of AI-assisted decision making: the goal is to close the gap between perceived and actual trustworthiness of AI systems so that users exhibit appropriate reliance on them. We argue that this approach, while useful for decision problems that are well-defined and clearly scoped, overly restricts what it means to make a decision with AI support. To overcome this limitation, we develop three dimensions of AI-assisted decision making. First, trusting AI is only one of several possible strategies for managing uncertainty. Second, trust calibration is often misapplied when AI models "large-world" decision problems, i.e., ill-defined situations where goals and states are only partially known or unknowable. Third, in such settings human-AI alignment requires addressing higher-order decision processes. We conclude by reflecting on the implications of our observations on the design of process-oriented human-AI coupled systems that jointly identify and negotiate uncertainty throughout the decision-making task.

classification.tldr: 批判性分析了信任校准框架在定义不明确决策场景中的局限，提出人机对齐需处理更高阶决策过程并设计面向过程的人机耦合系统。

papers.title: Trust Hinders Bidirectional Human-AI Alignment

papers.abstractEn: We present HiPAD, a single fusion network submitted to all six sub-tracks of the MPDD-AVG 2026 depression-detection challenge, covering the Elder and Young cohorts and three modality sets (gait, audio-visual, and both), each combined with personality descriptions. The network encodes each available modality with a shared BiLSTM, zero-pads absent modalities, and applies cross-modal attention only when at least two of gait, audio and video are present. Personality, which dominates our results, is kept out of the attention and fused by concatenation. Because the architecture is identical in every sub-track, differences between them reflect the data rather than the model, and we use this to study three questions. Our main finding is that the personality description, roughly 150 tokens about who the subject is, carries more depression signal than audio, video, and gait combined: gait plus personality alone (TLS 0.647) beats every configuration that includes audio and video. First, a four-level ablation of the personality description (L0-L3) quantifies this: removing every personality-derived feature, including the Big Five scores that earlier MPDD ablations keep, lowers the Track-Level Score by 0.499 to 0.507 and leaves the model at chance. Second, domain-adapting the personality encoder with LoRA (7B) or QLoRA (72B) on PHQ-8/9 data raises binary Cohen's $κ$ by 0.13 but lowers the overall score by distorting the PHQ-9 regression; a frozen RoBERTa-large encoder does better at this sample size. Third, at fixed architecture, handcrafted clinical features (eGeMAPS, OpenFace action units) outperform generic deep features (wav2vec2, DenseNet) on the audio-visual tracks. The unified system reaches a cross-track G-Score of 0.482; with under 100 subjects per cohort, the limiting factors are the size of the representation and the calibration of the outputs, not the choice of architecture.

classification.tldr: 提出融合步态、音视频与人格描述的统一多模态网络用于抑郁检测，发现人格文本信号超过其他模态，并量化人格消融与领域微调的校准局限。

papers.title: HiPAD: A Unified Gait, Audio-Visual, and Personality Fusion Network for Depression Detection, with a Hierarchical Personality Ablation and the Calibration Limits of Domain-Adapted LLMs

papers.abstractEn: Claims of recursive self-improvement are easy to make and hard to falsify: did improvement come from re-using designer-provided mechanisms, or from mechanisms the system authored itself? We introduce a pre-registered, two-tier accounting: M1 counts machine-generated content instances within a designer-provided vocabulary, while M2 counts machine-authored mechanism types (new operators registered into the runtime's own vocabulary, with a held-out-validation certificate). We report the first audited M2 genesis events. In the primary event, depth-limited compositional search over elementary operators, judged by held-out R^2 on real NIST hydrogen Balmer measurements, produced the operator sq(inv(n)) = 1/n^2 -- the Rydberg-level form -- which no standard-library transform could express (held-out R^2: -0.546 best standard transform vs. 1.0000000 composed). A protocol flaw (independent variable built by inverting the very law under test) was caught in audit and repaired via an independent-label protocol; extrapolation to unseen levels (n=8,9 trained on n<=7) attains relative error ~10^-6, four to six orders beyond the best standard operator. A second event independently recovered sqrt(inv(a)) -- Kepler's velocity law -- from JPL ephemeris vectors. Also incorporated: an audited compounding channel (first domain-level measurement: 1.109x accuracy ratio on a real held-out domain) and blind, decurated genesis exams whose honest tally is zero. The Kepler event passes line audit; the hydrogen gap reproduces on He II; the certificate is threshold-stable. Against eleven prior systems, the contribution is the measurement and governance of machine-authored mechanisms, not the search algorithm or rediscovered physics. Limitations: exams were curated by agents who knew the textbook answer, triggers manual, grammar observer-injected; both events demonstrate capability to author, not yet autonomous genesis.

classification.tldr: 提出预注册的双层核算协议来审计递归自我改进中机器自创机制的真实性，并报告了首个经审计的机器自创算子事件。

papers.title: Pre-Registered Genesis Accounting for Recursive Self-Improvement: First Audited Operator-Genesis Events in a Physics-Discovery Runtime

papers.abstractEn: Industrial IoT sensors produce continuous, high-volume data streams that predictive maintenance needs to analyse in real time. Cloud-centric architectures send all raw telemetry to central servers, which costs latency, bandwidth and resilience. This paper presents a hybrid cloud-edge architecture for manufacturing predictive maintenance built on AWS IoT Core and AWS IoT Greengrass v2, with local machine learning inference at the edge and selective cloud synchronization. We deploy two configurations on real AWS infrastructure and compare them: a cloud-only baseline (Configuration A) and the proposed hybrid edge architecture (Configuration B). We measure end-to-end inference latency, bandwidth consumption and inference accuracy. Configuration B cuts cloud-bound bandwidth by 86.8% (63.6 KB to 7.2 KB per 200-reading window) and decision latency by 256x (23.1 ms cloud round trip to 0.09 ms local inference). At the edge, with no cloud involvement, it keeps an anomaly-class F1 score of 0.84 and 91% recall. The evaluation also instruments system uptime and Stream Manager queuing under cloud disconnection; the quantitative disconnection experiment is left as planned work. Our review of the literature points to four gaps that this work addresses: the lack of empirically validated Greengrass v2 deployments for predictive maintenance, unquantified bandwidth savings from selective edge synchronization, unmeasured resilience under cloud disconnection, and the open MLOps feedback loop at the edge.

classification.tldr: 提出基于AWS Greengrass的云边混合预测性维护推理架构，实测将带宽降低86.8%、决策延迟降低256倍并保持异常检测精度。

papers.title: Seamless Deployment of Machine Learning Inference at the Far Edge: An Empirical AWS IoT Greengrass Architecture for Industrial Predictive Maintenance

papers.abstractEn: Dengue is a viral infection caused by the dengue virus (DENV) and a major public health concern in Bangladesh, where symptom overlap with other febrile illnesses complicates early diagnosis. This study compares Logistic Regression, Random Forest and XGBoost to predict dengue from clinical and hematological data using two Bangladeshi hospital datasets (2024, n=1,511; 2025, n=1,283) with SMOTE. Extended models outperformed benchmarks within 2024 (Random Forest ROC-AUC 0.640 to 0.661), with RDW-CV the most consistently influential added predictor. 2025 benchmark performance was higher (ROC-AUC 0.904), unexplained by class imbalance and possibly reflecting data quality. External validation is needed.

classification.tldr: 比较多种机器学习模型利用临床和血液学数据预测孟加拉国登革热感染，扩展特征模型略有提升但外部验证仍需开展。

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Dengue Infection Using Clinical and Hematological Data from Bangladesh: A Comparative Analysis of Benchmark and Extended Prediction Models

papers.abstractEn: Large language model (LLM)-based AI Scientists advance scientific discovery, yet they suffer from inefficiencies due to noisy observations. Existing principle-evolving agents act on every anomaly, leaving its source unresolved: a new mechanism or an evaluation artifact, so invalid revisions bias evolution. To address this, we formulate revision as evidence admission: anomalies steer search immediately, but only independently verified evidence may rewrite persistent principles, and contradicted principles are retracted. We realize this in TRIAGE-PIEVO , which pairs an anomaly-responsive search portfolio with a staged verification gate that alone controls what enters principle state. Across four scientific tasks with three backbones, TRIAGE-PIEVO (1) attains the highest average solution quality with +7.5%~11.8% over the strongest baseline per backbone, matching the strongest baseline's full-budget quality with one-third of the evaluation budget on Qwen3-235B; and additional stress tests and cross-harness deployment demonstrate that (2) in constructed stress tests, it admits none of the corrupted, hidden-source, or exploit evidence that ungated variants admit, while missing no planted mechanism, and (3) plugged unchanged into three external research harnesses, it cuts false evidence admissions by over 60% and raises verified scores by 31%~43%.

classification.tldr: 提出将科学发现agent的原理修订建模为证据准入问题，通过分阶段验证门控只允许经独立验证的证据改写持久原理，在四个科学任务上提升解质量并大幅减少虚假证据准入。

papers.title: Triage-PiEvo: Evidence Admission for Principle-Evolving Scientific Agents

papers.abstractEn: Mixed-variable optimization in scientific discovery often requires exploring large combinatorial spaces under costly experimental evaluations, making sample?efficient Bayesian optimization (BO) essential. However, existing BO methods typ?ically rely on structural descriptors to define similarity among categorical variables, implicitly assuming that structural similarity reflects similarity in task performance. In scientific optimization, this assumption is often violated, leading to surrogate representations that are poorly aligned with the optimization objective. To address this limitation, we propose TagBO (Task-aware Graph Bayesian Optimization), a method that integrates LLM-derived relational priors with descriptor-based struc?tural information for mixed-variable Bayesian optimization. Rather than directly using LLM outputs as predictive scores, TagBO treats LLM outputs as a potentially noisy source of task-aware relational priors and extracts coarse ordinal relational signals from LLM reasoning to construct task-aware similarity structures for scien?tific optimization. TagBO then performs constrained Gaussian process Bayesian optimization over the resulting joint discrete-continuous representation space. Ex?periments on diverse chemistry and materials formulation tasks demonstrate that TagBO consistently improves sample efficiency under fixed evaluation budgets across LLMs of varying capabilities.

classification.tldr: 提出任务感知的图贝叶斯优化方法，将大模型推理中提取的序数关系信号作为噪声先验来构建变量相似性结构，在化学与材料配方优化中显著提升样本效率。

papers.title: TagBO: LLM-Driven Task-Aware Graph Bayesian Optimization for Scientific Discovery

papers.abstractEn: Chiplet technology is a key approach for extending Moore's Law. However, its design process is constrained by two primary challenges: the scarcity of early-stage platforms for rapidly evaluating chiplet-based heterogeneous systems, and the complex relationships between design parameters and optimization metrics. To address these challenges, we propose a synergistic framework that integrates a Large Language Model (LLM) with Bayesian Optimization (BO), enabling architectural-level simulation and automated optimization for the 2.5D/3D CPU-GPU heterogeneous chiplets. We extend the open-source chiplet simulator to evaluate 3D designs by supporting graph topologies. Further, to enhance the exploration efficiency of BO, we introduce an LLM that generates high-quality policies to guide the optimization process, enabled by our proposed adaptive directional policy reasoning (ADPR) and an exploration gain-aware fine-tuning method. Finally, we use the policy-guided BO to perform an automated and efficient exploration of the complex chiplet design space. Experiments on 2.5D and 3D chiplet reveal that our framework improves design space exploration efficiency.

classification.tldr: 将大模型与贝叶斯优化结合用于2.5D/3D异构芯粒架构设计空间探索，通过自适应方向性策略推理生成引导策略以提升优化效率。

papers.title: LLM-Augmented Bayesian Optimization with Adaptive Policies for Chiplet Design Space Exploration

papers.abstractEn: ScienceBuddy-PV adapts the ScienceBuddy recursive-in-recursive design to panvascular intervention research through a structured evidence ledger, device-vessel ontology, abstention contract and retained failure bank. Recursive harness optimization and outer-loop model learning, including reinforcement learning, are specified but not executed. We audit a fixed component, rather than the complete agent system, using separate ARCADE syntax and stenosis tasks (1,000 training, 200 validation and 300 test images per task). A shared task-masked convolutional model was trained once per representation setting; its parameters and the heuristic support gate were then held fixed, with the stenosis threshold selected on validation data. On the locked test sets, syntax Dice was 0.475 (95% CI 0.459-0.490) and stenosis Dice was 0.231 (95% CI 0.214-0.249). Stenosis pixel AUROC was 0.957 and AUPRC was 0.180 at prevalence 0.00975. The gate accepted 76.7% of stenosis-frame outputs versus 100% for a score-only comparator. In a constructed mask audit, it accepted 44.3% of reference candidates and rejected 55.7%, exposing the cost of abstention. Acceptance does not establish correctness or clinical safety. This public-data component audit makes support and abstention measurable and provides a reproducible protocol for future collaborative agent studies. It does not demonstrate recursive improvement, patient-level validity or clinical device recommendations.

classification.tldr: 该论文面向泛血管介入研究提出了带证据账本与弃答机制的递归式智能体改进协议,并对固定组件进行了可复现的审计评估,量化了支持与弃答的表现。

papers.title: ScienceBuddy-PV: A Verifier-Governed Recursive Improvement Protocol for Panvascular Intervention Research

papers.abstractEn: We propose a controlled Large Language Model (LLM) workflow for explaining risk score differences using similar historical transactions. The workflow combines reference retrieval and contrastive SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) evidence with reference-based LLM reasoning and deterministic validation. Experiments on a test dataset show that the workflow produces more consistent, evidence-grounded and traceable diagnoses than the same LLM without structured workflow guidance.

classification.tldr: 该论文设计了一个受控LLM工作流，结合相似交易检索、对比SHAP证据与确定性验证，用于解释风险评分差异，实验表明其诊断结果比无结构引导的LLM更一致、更有据可溯。

papers.title: A Controlled LLM Workflow for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis of Risk Score Differences

papers.abstractEn: While language therapy is the primary treatment for post-stroke aphasia, limited clinical resources often restrict patient access to proper care. Addressing this gap requires reliable training simulations for medical professionals. However, current AI efforts focus almost exclusively on speech processing, leaving speech generation largely unexplored. This study introduces AphaVoice, a novel text-to-speech (TTS) framework explicitly engineered to synthesize highly realistic aphasic speech. Evaluated against state-of-the-art TTS systems, AphaVoice demonstrates a superior ability to capture the clinical feature of dysfluency, outperforming existing models in temporal metrics while consistently maintaining speaker identity. By leveraging latent space shifting, the model also supports multi-speaker generation without sacrificing phonetic realism. Ultimately, AphaVoice provides a scalable, high-fidelity tool for medical training and clinical simulation related to aphasia.

classification.tldr: 构建可合成失真失流畅失语语音的文本转语音框架，为失语症医疗培训提供高保真模拟工具。

papers.title: AphaVoice: Text-to-Speech Model for Aphasia Patient Simulation

papers.abstractEn: Scientific research increasingly depends on curating experimental data from literature. Scientific data curation requires verifying exact experimental conditions (e.g., specific assays, clinical outcomes, and data availability) across long, heterogeneous files, which is a highly time-consuming process. Existing benchmarks evaluate only broad relevance on short queries, failing to capture this complexity. We introduce SciCurateBench, a benchmark of 200 expert-annotated papers from major life-science journals that challenges systems to verify conjunctive biological experimental criteria from raw, unprocessed scientific literature. We show that plain LLMs and popular reasoning, tool-using, and feedback-based agents all struggle with this task. To study what makes the task tractable, we further propose LangPoli, an integrative system in which a policy agent generates natural language action guidelines that actor agents convert into executable tools. LangPoli showed strong performance on both Paper Classification (83.16% F1 vs. 58.22% for its base LLM) and Structured Information Retrieval, and also improves re-ranking on the public benchmarks of LitSearch, BEIR, and TREC. We further explore curriculum transfer, a method that distills generalizable strategies from solved tasks to accelerate the solving of related problems. We hope this work facilitates research in truly practical scientific AI assistance. The anonymized pre-release can be found from https://anonymous.4open. science/r/scicuratebench-D885/.

classification.tldr: 该工作构建了从异质科学文献中核验实验数据标准的专家标注基准，并提出将语言动作转化为可执行工具的多智能体系统，显著提升分类与结构化信息检索性能。

papers.title: SciCurateBench: Curating Experimental Data from Heterogeneous Scientific Literature with Verbal-Action Agents

papers.abstractEn: Test-time adaptation (TTA) enables time series forecasters to update after deployment as new observations become available. However, adaptation objectives that focus primarily on prediction errors at individual time steps do not fully address the needs of financial time series forecasting. In addition to pointwise return fitting, return direction and the price trajectories reconstructed from sequences of returns are also important. To better account for these properties, we introduce Direction- and Price-Aware Adaptation Loss (DPAL), which combines pointwise return fitting with directional and price-calibration terms. We apply DPAL within existing TSF-TTA frameworks without modifying the source forecaster or the adapter architecture. Across a diverse collection of financial datasets, DPAL reduces reconstructed-price mean squared error in most evaluated settings.

classification.tldr: 提出兼顾收益率方向与价格轨迹校准的测试时自适应损失，可嵌入现有时序预测TTA框架，在多数金融数据集上降低重建价格误差。

papers.title: DPAL: A Test-Time Adaptation Loss for Financial Time Series Forecasting

papers.abstractEn: Comics are one of the great visual records of the twentieth century: hundreds of thousands of pages in which a mass readership saw its leaders, its wars and its heroes. Most of this record has never been studied as a whole; comics scholarship proceeds one book at a time. We argue that artificial intelligence, including generative models, can change this to the benefit of the medium itself. We propose PAGE, a framework that makes artificial intelligence an instrument for comics research. It parses every scan into panels, text and a bibliographic record; annotates each page with a vision-language model that follows a written codebook, as a human coder would; grounds samples of these readings in human annotation; and explains change across an archive, with estimates controlled for publisher and genre. We demonstrate the framework on 3,929 American comic books (1938--1956) and 87 volumes of Japanese manga, in three studies, each resting on a different capability. The first pairs text search with visual reading to recover how a mass medium portrayed political power. The second measures the page's visual form across an industry and recovers the hand of individual artists. The third follows who speaks across two comics traditions, checked against human annotation. Beyond research, the same instruments can make archives searchable by what is drawn, open comics to blind and low-vision readers, and help preserve fragile collections and credit uncredited artists. We outline a research agenda in which artificial intelligence strengthens the study, preservation and reach of the medium.

classification.tldr: 提出用视觉语言模型对漫画进行大规模自动标注与统计分析的PAGE框架，在近四千本美国漫画和87卷日漫上验证了AI辅助漫画研究的可行性。

papers.title: Studying Comics at Scale with Artificial Intelligence: The PAGE Framework and Three Studies of American Comics and Japanese Manga

papers.abstractEn: In clinical practice, experts often begin by converting raw inputs into a set of expert features before making a decision. While black-box models trained on raw input can outperform models trained on expert views, it remains unclear what predictive signal the raw model exploits beyond what the expert view captures. We introduce an audit framework to quantify this gap using Shared Canonical Component Removal (SCCR). Unlike standard residualization or concept erasure, SCCR selectively removes only those directions strongly shared between learned raw and expert embeddings. Evaluations on synthetic data, coronary artery disease (CAD) detection, antidepressant treatment dropout prediction, and skin lesion classification using SkinCon annotations show that SCCR identifies the ways in which expert views are insufficient and recovers residual predictive signal while minimizing redundancy with the expert view.

classification.tldr: 提出SCCR审计框架，通过仅移除原始表示与专家表示强共享的方向来量化专家视角之外模型利用的预测信号，并在多个临床任务上验证。

papers.title: Shared Canonical Component Removal Beyond Expert Views

papers.abstractEn: Many machine learning approaches are two-level: an expert selects a class of methods, within this class the choice of key components is critical and usually manual. This paper addresses the automatic tuning of these components and proposes a framework transferable across models of different nature. The multi-agent large language model (LLM) framework has three roles---analyst, coder, and recorder~---with an experiment log and a sandboxed execution environment. Unlike systems that optimize the entire ML script or search architectures in a discrete space, the framework operates over an open but semantically narrow space: the agent generates code only for the specified components, leaving the overall network structure unchanged. The approach is validated in two directions: tuning a classification spiking neural network with correlation learning, and solving high-order differential equations with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN). Across five tasks---spiking classification on MNIST and Digits, and boundary-value problems for the generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky (KS) equations---the agent outperforms the baselines: classification accuracy is 13 percentage points (MNIST) and 6 percentage points (Digits) higher; the error against the analytical single-soliton solution is reduced approximately 2491-fold; the invariant-preservation error drops approximately 325-fold in the selected GNLSE run with a Gaussian perturbation and by more than 100-fold on average over repeated initializations; and the mass drift drops 14-fold for the KS problem with a Gaussian perturbation. The framework thus tunes key components on tasks of different nature without changing its internal structure.

classification.tldr: 提出由分析员、编码员和记录员组成的多智能体LLM框架，自动调优专用神经网络的关键组件，在脉冲网络分类与PINN求解微分方程任务上显著优于基线。

papers.title: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Automated Tuning of Specialized Neural Network Models

papers.abstractEn: Machine learning models are increasingly used for automated feature extraction from weakly annotated bioimaging data, such as microscopy and cytomorphology images. Due to the sole dependency of automated feature extraction, existing methods yield inconsistent classification performance across weakly annotated datasets. Here, we propose a model-agnostic knowledge augmentation method that enables ML models to exploit domain knowledge beyond what automated feature extraction can capture. The proposed approach improves classification performance across seven ML architectures. When integrated with masked autoencoder-based self-supervised learning, our method achieves the strongest overall performance, improving precision by 2.9% over the next-best method on three in-house microscopy datasets and by an average of 6.8% across three public cytomorphology benchmarks. We perform nucleus-level classification based on mislocalization of TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) from the nucleus to the cytoplasm, a phenotype linked to Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), using three independent microscopy datasets of motor neurons derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells. Accurate quantification of this phenotype at scale remains challenging and may contribute to inconsistencies across studies. Application of the best-performing model to these microscopy datasets reveals biological interpretations related to ALS, including dose-dependent effects of the proteasomal stressor, MG132, and the oxidative stressor, sodium arsenite (SA), on TDP-43 mislocalization, variable pathology in motor neurons from sporadic and familial ALS donors, and a lack of protection of the pharmacological compounds, edaravone and niclosamide, against SA-induced TDP-43 mislocalization. Together, our pipeline enables in-vitro cellular image analysis to advance understanding of ALS-associated pathology and potential treatments.

classification.tldr: 提出一种模型无关的知识增强方法，将领域知识注入弱标注生物图像分类流程，在显微镜和细胞形态学数据集上提升分类精度并用于ALS病理的定量分析。

papers.title: Model-agnostic Knowledge Augmented Machine Learning for Weakly Annotated Bioimaging Data

papers.abstractEn: We present a suite of 50 unpublished research-level theoretical physics problems with verifiable answers. Without AI assistance, a typical problem in our collection could be solved by a world expert in about a day or less but would take considerably longer for experts in adjacent specialties. We test the ability of off-the-shelf AI agents to tackle these problems autonomously, without human hints. When given access to tools available in a realistic setting, including the ability to search the literature and write scripts for numerical and symbolic work, the best-performing agent, GPT-6-Astra harnessed in Codex, obtains the final answers with a near-perfect accuracy of 98% at an average cost under USD 3 per problem. On average, agents show only small changes in accuracy when denied web search and access to background research papers, suggesting significant memorization of the literature. These results suggest that state-of-the-art agents can accurately perform concrete calculations required across theoretical physics research. We comment on the broader implications of these findings and discuss possible explanations for the current lack of agent-led breakthroughs in theoretical physics despite their outstanding problem-solving abilities.

classification.tldr: 构建50道可验证答案的研究级理论物理题目评测自主智能体，发现最强智能体准确率接近98%，但也暴露其对文献的强记忆依赖。

papers.title: TheoPhysEval: Assessing AI agents at autonomous theoretical physics problem solving

papers.abstractEn: Long-term personalized tutoring requires language models to translate a learner's evolving history into appropriate instructional support. Existing LLM-based tutoring systems use memory and retrieval to personalize responses, but the pedagogical rationale linking historical evidence to teaching strategies is not always explicit. We introduce RegulaTutor, a theory-informed framework for long-term personalized tutoring that connects historical evidence, learner interpretation, and learner-facing instruction. Guided by self-regulated learning (SRL) research, its tutoring harness operationalizes a cognitive, affective, metacognitive, and motivational (CAMM) framework for deriving evidence-supported learner interpretations and teaching policies. The resulting policies retain links to their supporting evidence and are updated as new observations arrive. This staged workflow also supports systematic refinement through PairRoute, an offline procedure that uses intermediate execution records to distinguish harness, model, and mixed failures. PairRoute proposes and evaluates targeted harness revisions, then constructs reviewed stage-level supervision for confirmed model failures remaining under the selected harness. We focus this refinement on historical evidence acquisition, which underpins personalized instruction and allows outputs to be checked against learning records and reference answers. RegulaTutor improves historical-evidence accuracy, learner diagnosis, and judged teaching quality on average across evaluated model configurations. PairRoute results show an endpoint improvement in standalone-model historical-evidence accuracy over the refinement trajectory. Together, these results highlight RegulaTutor's potential to support lifelong personalized education through instructional policies that evolve with learner histories and targeted improvements to the tutoring system.

classification.tldr: 提出基于自我调节学习理论的长期个性化辅导框架，将学习者历史证据与教学策略关联并持续更新，提升诊断与教学质量。

papers.title: RegulaTutor: A Theory-Informed Framework for Long-Term Personalized Learning

papers.abstractEn: AI-assisted scientific discovery increasingly seeks to move beyond generating plausible ideas toward reproducible, constraint-aware workflows that can support practical engineering decisions. We present MARS, a hierarchical Multi-Agent Reasoning System for knowledge-grounded material substitution under scientific and manufacturing constraints. We apply MARS to replace per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), a demanding materials-design problem in which substitutes must satisfy functional performance, environmental, experimental, and processing requirements. MARS decomposes substitution into a closed-loop workflow comprising requirement analysis, grounded candidate generation, and manufacturability assessment with process design. The system integrates retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge-graph reasoning, a database of lab-available materials, persistent memory of intermediate results, and rejection-aware iterative feedback. In a PFAS-substitution case study, MARS generates structured material requirements, identifies an evidence-grounded substitute candidate, and develops a lab-scale manufacturing route. In a multi-seed ablation evaluation, MARS achieves the highest overall performance across all three subsystems, with gains that persist when the backbone model is held fixed. These results suggest that hierarchical decomposition, knowledge grounding, and manufacturability-aware refinement improve material-substitution reasoning beyond model capability alone.

classification.tldr: 提出层次化多智能体推理系统，结合检索增强、知识图谱推理与持久记忆，在PFAS替代的材料设计任务中实现约束感知且可复现的科学发现工作流。

papers.title: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reasoning Systems for Knowledge-Grounded Material Substitution

papers.abstractEn: Widely reused preprocessing pipelines for electronic health records can encode assumptions about when information became available, what clinical episode a label represents, and what missingness means. These assumptions are rarely audited systematically and may propagate across subsequent studies when preprocessing pipelines are reused or adapted. Using MIMIC-IV as a case study, we identify and quantify violations of three complementary forms of preprocessing alignment, i.e., temporal, semantic, and population alignment, which manifest as temporal leakage, feature-task misalignment, and biased imputation. We show how ambiguities in timestamp semantics, episode definitions, endpoint construction, modality selection, and missingness handling can alter the information available to a model and affect the interpretation of its predictions. Through analyses of MIMIC-IV data and empirical case studies, we demonstrate that such choices may remain largely invisible in aggregate predictive performance while changing the signals on which models rely. We derive practical recommendations for temporally valid, clinically aligned, and reproducible preprocessing of MIMIC-IV and related electronic health record datasets. The code for our experiments, including our proposed preprocessing, is available at: https://github.com/m2l-lab/mimic-iv-preprocess.

classification.tldr: 该文系统审计了临床机器学习中电子病历预处理流程的时间、语义与人群对齐问题，量化了数据泄漏与偏差如何隐蔽地改变模型依赖的信号，并提出可复现的预处理建议。

papers.title: Hidden Data Challenges in Clinical Machine Learning

papers.abstractEn: A defined-benefit pension is only as safe as its sponsor, yet sponsor distress is under-instrumented relative to plan-side modelling. We present a transparent, reproducible early-warning pipeline built entirely on public data. A Sponsor Vulnerability Index (SVI), a gradient-boosted classifier over point-in-time SEC EDGAR balance-sheet fundamentals and two macro series, predicts a filings-based distress state one to two quarters ahead. On 36 U.S. sponsors in five sector groups (1,418 firm-quarters, 2015Q1-2025Q3) it reaches an out-of-fold AUC-ROC of 0.887 and PR-AUC of 0.711 (base rate 11.9%) under leave-one-firm-out cross-validation. A Monte Carlo VaR with a stylized transition-stress overlay shows that climate-type stress is negligible for a diversified plan but adds 20-43% to one-year 95% VaR when 22.5% of assets are held in sponsor securities. A dynamic self-investment cap maps the SVI to a limit that falls from 8% to below 1% in acute distress and recovers with the sponsor, which we illustrate on PG&E's 2019 bankruptcy and Boeing's persistent fragility. We report the method's failure modes alongside its results (book-equity labels that also fire on non-credit events such as spin-offs, positives concentrated in one firm, and stylized stress parameters) and release code, data and results under a concept DOI.

classification.tldr: 基于公开SEC文件构建梯度提升的养老金发起人困境早期预警指数，并结合压力情景VaR与动态自我投资上限，AUC达0.887。

papers.title: Early Detection of Pension-Sponsor Distress from Public Filings: A Sponsor Vulnerability Index, Stress-Augmented VaR, and Dynamic Self-Investment Caps

papers.abstractEn: Cancer diagnosis and treatment increasingly rely on multi-modal diagnostic technologies that generate high-dimensional datasets. Although these datasets are rich in pathological information, they pose considerable challenges in interpretation, dimensionality reduction, and clinical applicability. Conventional machine learning approaches often fail to extract meaningful cross-modal features, thereby limiting predictive accuracy in patient risk stratification. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an unsupervised machine learning framework that integrates feature extraction, tensor decomposition, and clustering to improve cancer risk prediction. The framework employs tensor decomposition to fuse heterogeneous genomic and clinical data, enabling the extraction of latent, biologically meaningful features that outperform unimodal feature sets. Multiple feature extraction strategies are investigated, and the resulting features are subsequently clustered using a range of clustering algorithms. Comparative evaluations based on internal and external metrics are then used to identify the most effective configurations. The framework is validated on LinkedOmics data comprising 11,158 patients across 32 cancer types. For patient risk stratification, clinically relevant attributes such as tumor purity, pathological stage, and survival outcomes serve as ground-truth indicators. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of tSVD+GMM, which consistently outperforms other configurations across clinical benchmarks.

classification.tldr: 提出基于张量分解与聚类的无监督多模态融合框架，整合基因组和临床数据用于癌症风险分层，在 32 种癌症的 11158 名患者数据上验证了 tSVD+GMM 的优势。

papers.title: Tensor-based Fusion of Multi-modal Data for Predicting Cancer Risk Levels

papers.abstractEn: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored as facilitators of group discussion and collaborative work, but the behavioral differences between LLM-generated and human facilitation remain insufficiently characterized. We compare human Project Manager facilitation turns from scenario-based collaborative design meetings with Llama 3.1 8B Instruct responses across 199 paired contexts from the AMI Meeting Corpus. The analysis covers five confirmatory dimensions: contextual semantic distance, a lexical elaboration proxy, empathyand-hedge lexical density, topic divergence, and phase-vocabulary alignment. An exploratory directiveness measure failed domain validation and is not interpreted. The sampled human Project Manager turns were higher on contextual semantic distance (r = 0.644) and on empathyand-hedge lexical density (r = 0.203). The second contrast is carried mainly by hedge terms, so we read it as lexical hedging rather than psychological empathy. Llama-generated facilitation was higher on topic divergence (r = 0.703), the lexical elaboration proxy (r = 0.288; lengthconfounded), and instruction-conditioned phase-vocabulary alignment (r = 0.382). A secondary no-phase check left the Llama-higher phase contrast in place. The system prompt still requested a facilitation move, so that check is not evidence of spontaneous phase awareness. These differences should not be interpreted as a ranking of facilitation quality. The resulting behavioral profile provides a reference point for later comparisons of LLM facilitators, human facilitators, prompts, models, and collaborative settings.

classification.tldr: 在协作设计会议语料上系统比较人类项目经理与Llama 3.1引导发言的行为差异，发现人类语义距离和模糊词密度更高，而模型话题发散度更高，为后续LLM引导者研究提供行为参照。

papers.title: Human and LLM Facilitation in Collaborative Design Meetings: A Computational Behavioral Comparison

papers.abstractEn: Technologies like large language models make it easier to convert cultural material into analyzable variables, while LLM-driven agentic systems extend machine assistance to other parts of the research workflow. Rather than a full how-to guide or an exhaustive review of recent LLM use cases, this chapter looks at some crucial aspects of this new paradigm as well as the bigger picture. I argue that these technologies expand the scale, methodological range, and scope for delegation, while the basic logic by which those measurements support cultural claims remains mostly unchanged.

classification.tldr: 该章节探讨大语言模型与智能体系统在文化分析中的应用范式，认为其扩展了研究规模与委托范围，但测量支撑文化论断的基本逻辑基本未变。

papers.title: Large Language Models, Machine-Assisted Cultural Analytics, and the Agentic Turn

papers.abstractEn: Background: Discontinuity in neonatal EEG is a critical marker of brain dysfunction but can be difficult to quantify visually. Inter-burst intervals (IBIs) are a key characteristic of discontinuity, yet their definition does not easily translate to AI detection. Objectives: To introduce low-voltage intervals (LVIs), defined exclusively by amplitude and duration, as a context-independent alternative to IBIs, develop an AI detection method for LVIs, and assess their clinical utility as a marker of brain injury. Methods: We developed a ConvNeXt model to detect LVIs and compared its performance with existing methods. We then tested the clinical relevance of detected LVIs across four applications: 1) grading background EEG abnormalities on an open benchmark dataset, 2) classifying clinical hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy (HIE) grades and comparing with a normal EEG dataset, 3) seizure prediction, and 4) association with seizure burden. Results: For training and validation, 654 hours of per-channel EEG from 123 neonates were reviewed and 51,162 LVIs were annotated. On held-out validation, ConvNeXt had an AUC of 0.996 and a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.926. Model-reader agreement exceeded inter-reader agreement ($Δκ= 0.025$, 95% CI: 0.007 to 0.045, $p<0.001$), attaining expert-level equivalence. On a combined dataset of 444 neonates, percentage LVI showed a strong association with EEG grades (Spearman's $ρ=0.801$), a moderate association with HIE grades ($ρ=0.384$), a weaker association with seizure burden ($ρ=0.244$), and a strong seizure prediction capacity (AUC $=0.872$). Conclusion: AI detection of LVIs achieves expert-level equivalence, whereas quantitative features do not. Automated LVI quantification provides a robust clinical biomarker of neonatal encephalopathy associated with background EEG activity, HIE severity, and seizure risk.

classification.tldr: 提出以幅度和时长定义的低电压区间作为新生儿脑病生物标志物，训练ConvNeXt检测模型达到专家级一致并验证其临床关联性。

papers.title: Expert-level detection of low-voltage intervals in EEG as a robust biomarker of neonatal encephalopathy

papers.abstractEn: Day-ahead electricity forecasts can help building operators schedule heating, ventilation, and other services around anticipated demand. Choosing a forecasting model also requires balancing accuracy with its forecast-time inputs, local training, and computational requirements. We benchmark statistical, machine-learning, recurrent neural-network, and pretrained TimesFM models for a university building. We use chronological validation and evaluate all configurations on the same 57 test days, comparing accuracy across workdays, weekends, and holidays alongside local fitting and forecasting time. Weather covariates use retrospective observations. TimesFM 3.0 with covariates achieves the lowest overall errors, reducing mean absolute error by approximately 43\% relative to weekly seasonal-naive forecasting. XGBoost remains competitive, although paired daily comparisons do not establish a clear mean-absolute-error advantage for TimesFM. TimesFM also performs strongly using only past electricity consumption. Adding covariates improves its holiday forecasts but slightly worsens workday and weekend forecasts, leaving overall mean absolute error almost unchanged. TimesFM requires no building-specific weight training, while XGBoost offers rapid local fitting and inference. The evaluated LSTM takes longer to fit without outperforming either approach. An exploratory historical evaluation reveals seasonal variation, while a separate weather-source comparison produces only small changes in the selected TimesFM configuration's accuracy. These results support pretrained TimesFM as a strong initial forecasting baseline for this building, with XGBoost as a competitive locally fitted alternative. Covariates are particularly useful when improved holiday forecasts justify the additional input preparation.

classification.tldr: 该文在大学建筑日前电力预测任务上系统比较了统计、机器学习与预训练TimesFM模型，发现带协变量的TimesFM整体误差最低，可作为强基线。

papers.title: Machine Learning and Time-Series Foundation Models for Day-Ahead Electricity Forecasting in a University Building

papers.abstractEn: Industrial risk-control systems typically rely on structured-data models for efficient prediction, yet substantial valuable information remains embedded in unstructured long text. Extracting this information through manual feature engineering is labor-intensive, while requiring a large language model (LLM) to process every real-time input may not meet practical deployment requirements. To address this challenge, we propose LLM-BlockFE, an LLM-guided offline feature construction framework that converts long text into executable feature programs, thereby avoiding LLM calls during online inference. LLM-BlockFE constructs feature programs by incrementally appending immutable code blocks and evaluates candidate features using a downstream model. To address the tendency of conventional greedy search to become trapped in suboptimal solutions, our method introduces a block-level rollback mechanism based on depth-calibrated credit allocation and advances multiple independent search trajectories in an interleaved manner, reducing redundant exploration by sharing fixed descriptions of each trajectory's exploration direction. After the search, the resulting programs are frozen and deployed to extract structured features for downstream prediction models. Across two public and two private datasets, LLM-BlockFE achieves absolute AUC improvements of 0.0069 to 0.0358 over the strongest baseline on each dataset in the full-dataset comparison. Post-launch monitoring across five deployed financial risk-control applications shows absolute KS improvements of 0.02 to 1.56 percentage points over the existing manually designed strategy.

classification.tldr: 该论文提出一种离线LLM引导的特征构建方法，将长文本转化为可执行特征程序以避免在线调用LLM，并在金融风控应用中显著提升下游预测模型的AUC与KS指标。

papers.title: Long Text to Predictive Features: LLM-Guided Blockwise Feature Engineering via Executable Program Search

papers.abstractEn: Machine learning (ML) in high-energy nuclear physics (HENP) is entering a new stage in which physical knowledge is incorporated more directly into data analysis, simulation, and physics inference. This mini-review focuses on developments that have matured in the past several years.
